# Fil One Documentation

> Fil One is S3-compatible object storage built for AI agents and data-intensive
> workloads. Stored on the Filecoin network, where storage providers must
> continuously submit cryptographic proofs that they still hold the data they
> committed to store. No egress fees on paid plans, no per-request charges,
> $4.99/TB/month with a $4.99/month minimum.
> Use any S3-compatible SDK or tool — point it at your region's endpoint,
> `https://<region>.s3.fil.one`, with standard Access Key ID / Secret Access Key
> auth. Endpoint, region and key must all refer to the same region.

Critical integration notes for developers:
- CreateBucket and DeleteBucket via the S3 API are region-dependent: supported
  in us-east-1, unavailable in eu-west-1 (use the dashboard there)
- Path-style addressing required: `https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one/bucket/key`
  (virtual-hosted-style URLs are not supported)
- Access keys are scoped to ONE region and cannot be used against another
- Region, versioning, Object Lock and retention are fixed at bucket creation and
  cannot be changed afterwards (no update-bucket operation)
- Authentication: AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) — all S3-compatible SDKs
  handle this automatically
- All buckets are private by default; all data is encrypted at rest and in
  transit (TLS); encryption cannot be disabled. At-rest encryption is done by the
  regional storage gateway and keys are held by the regional operator, NOT by Fil
  One and NOT customer-managed. Do not name a specific cipher or SSE mode.
  SSE-KMS is rejected in BOTH regions (InvalidRequest in us-east-1; AccessDenied
  or InvalidRequest in eu-west-1) and SSE-C is unsupported — send no encryption
  headers at all. In eu-west-1, Get/PutBucketEncryption also return AccessDenied,
  so no encryption configuration can be read or written there
- Regions: eu-west-1 Europe (France, default) and us-east-1 US East (Michigan)
- Deletion is permanent and immediate on non-versioned buckets (no recycle bin).
  On versioned buckets a plain delete places a delete marker and prior versions
  are retained and still billed
- CopyObject / server-side copy is confirmed working in us-east-1, including
  copying a specific version onto the current key to promote it (a version
  restore). In eu-west-1 PLAIN COPY WORKS but the version-id form is UNVERIFIED
  (the harness cannot configure versioning over the API there); download and
  re-upload is the fallback. The dashboard has no restore/roll-back button either way
- Per-object CIDs, deal IDs, and sealing state are NOT exposed — customers
  cannot independently audit an individual object
- Paid past_due status is READ-ONLY immediately: writes are blocked from the
  moment a payment fails, not after a later deadline; the ~30-day window is
  retrieval-only before the account is disabled
- Trial caps are enforcement thresholds, not allowances: storage reaching 1 TB
  WRITE-LOCKS the account; egress reaching 2 TB DISABLES it entirely. Trial
  egress is a single cumulative budget over the 30 days. Enforced by a
  twice-daily job (~07:00/19:00 UTC), not in real time
- Storage is DECIMAL: 1 TB = 1,000 GB, 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes
- Governance Object Lock has NO grantable bypass permission in the product
- PutObjectRetention (per-object retention) is offered as a key permission and
  is confirmed working in us-east-1 (including Governance-mode bypass); not
  yet confirmed in eu-west-1 — use the bucket-level default retention there
- Legal Hold (GetObjectLegalHold/PutObjectLegalHold) is confirmed working in
  us-east-1, incl. blocking delete while a hold is active; not yet confirmed
  in eu-west-1
- Object/part size limits (5 TB object, 5 GB single-PUT, 10,000 parts, 5 MB min
  part) are standard AWS S3 values, NOT independently confirmed for Fil One
- Bucket names forbid dots (unlike AWS S3); object key max is 1,024 bytes
- In eu-west-1, UNIMPLEMENTED OPERATIONS RETURN AccessDenied (403), NOT
  NotImplemented (501), and a bucket/key you cannot see returns 403 instead of
  404. A 403 from PutBucketVersioning, PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketAcl,
  PutBucketEncryption, PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration or the tagging operations
  means the FEATURE IS ABSENT, not that the key lacks a permission
- ACL requests fail two different ways in eu-west-1: a canned-ACL HEADER on an
  upload (--acl public-read) is SILENTLY IGNORED and the upload SUCCEEDS, while a
  DEDICATED call (Put/GetBucketAcl, Put/GetObjectAcl) is REJECTED with
  AccessDenied. Neither makes an object public
- Error CODES deviate from AWS in eu-west-1 even though the XML format is
  standard: BadDigest->InvalidArgument, InvalidRange->InvalidArgument,
  InvalidTag->BadRequest, BucketAlreadyExists->BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou. Some
  invalid requests are also ACCEPTED where AWS returns 400
- Open eu-west-1 client-affecting bugs: ListObjects NextMarker can carry an
  internal suffix (use ListObjectsV2 + ContinuationToken instead);
  EncodingType=url encodes a space as "+" not "%20"; additional-checksum
  operations are unreliable (ChecksumType may be missing from
  CompleteMultipartUpload responses)
- Bucket Intelligence (RAG) is EARLY ACCESS and allowlisted, not GA


---

# Welcome to Fil One

Fil One is an S3-compatible object storage platform designed for teams that need
reliable, cost-effective storage with built-in compliance features. If you've used
AWS S3, you already know how to use Fil One.

## Why Fil One

**S3-compatible from day one.** Use the tools you already know — AWS CLI, boto3,
any S3-compatible SDK. Point your existing code at our endpoint and it works.

**Backed by Filecoin.** Fil One stores your data on Filecoin, a distributed
storage network where storage providers must continuously submit cryptographic
proofs that they are still holding the data they committed to store, or face
penalties. Note that this proof cycle is a property of the network — Fil One does
not expose per-object CIDs, deal IDs, or sealing state, so an individual object
cannot be independently audited by the customer today.

**No egress fees on paid plans.** On a paid plan there are no data-transfer
charges. (The free trial has a 2 TB egress cap.)

**Simple, flat pricing.** $4.99 / TB / month, with a $4.99 / month minimum. No
per-request charges, no hidden fees, no tiered pricing.

**30-day free trial.** 1 TB of storage and 2 TB of bandwidth, no credit card
required.


---

# Quickstart

Source: https://docs.fil.one/quickstart

This guide walks you through creating an account, setting up credentials, and
uploading your first object.

## 1. Create your account

1. Go to app.fil.one and sign up with your email or SSO.
2. Verify your email address.
3. No credit card needed — your 30-day free trial starts automatically.

## 2. Create a bucket

From the dashboard, click **New bucket**, then **Create bucket**. Give it a name
(lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens — no dots, unlike AWS S3) and choose
your settings:

- Region: eu-west-1 Europe (France, default) or us-east-1 US East (Michigan)
- Encryption: Always on (all data is encrypted at rest by default)
- Versioning: off by default
- Object Lock: off by default, requires versioning
- Retention: off by default, requires Object Lock

Region, versioning, Object Lock and retention are ALL fixed at creation. They
cannot be changed on an existing bucket and a bucket cannot be moved between
regions — you would have to create a new bucket and copy the data across.

The three object settings nest and are enabled in order: versioning first
(Object Lock is greyed out until it is on), then Object Lock (retention is greyed
out until it is on), then retention. Retention modes: Governance (default — in
standard S3 a bypass permission can override it, but Fil One exposes no grantable
bypass permission, so in practice it protects for the retention period) and
Compliance (no one, including the account owner, can delete or modify objects
until the retention period expires). Duration is set in days or years, from 1 day
up to 100 years.

You will also see an API key section during bucket creation. You can create a new
API key here or configure permissions for an existing one. A key belongs to a
single region and must match the bucket's region.

## 3. Upload your first object

Go to **API Keys** in the left menu and click **Create new key**. You'll get two values:

- **Access Key ID** — identifies your account (safe to store in config)
- **Secret Access Key** — authenticates your requests (treat like a password)

Your secret key is shown once. Copy it and store it securely. If you lose it,
you'll need to generate a new key pair.

### AWS CLI

```bash
aws configure set aws_access_key_id YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
aws configure set aws_secret_access_key YOUR_SECRET_KEY
aws configure set default.region eu-west-1

aws s3 cp my-file.txt s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one

aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/ --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

### Python (boto3)

```python
import boto3

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one",
    aws_access_key_id="YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    aws_secret_access_key="YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
)

s3.upload_file("my-file.txt", "my-bucket", "my-file.txt")

response = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="my-bucket")
for obj in response.get("Contents", []):
    print(obj["Key"], obj["Size"])
```

### JavaScript (AWS SDK v3)

```javascript
import { S3Client, PutObjectCommand, ListObjectsV2Command } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";

const client = new S3Client({
  endpoint: "https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one",
  region: "eu-west-1",
  forcePathStyle: true,
  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    secretAccessKey: "YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
  },
});

await client.send(new PutObjectCommand({
  Bucket: "my-bucket",
  Key: "my-file.txt",
  Body: readFileSync("my-file.txt"),
}));

const { Contents } = await client.send(
  new ListObjectsV2Command({ Bucket: "my-bucket" })
);
Contents?.forEach((obj) => console.log(obj.Key, obj.Size));
```

### Go (aws-sdk-go-v2)

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "strings"

    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/aws"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3"
)

func main() {
    client := s3.New(s3.Options{
        BaseEndpoint: aws.String("https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one"),
        Region:       "eu-west-1",
        UsePathStyle: true,
        Credentials: credentials.NewStaticCredentialsProvider(
            os.Getenv("FIL_ACCESS_KEY"),
            os.Getenv("FIL_SECRET_KEY"),
            "",
        ),
    })

    ctx := context.Background()

    client.PutObject(ctx, &s3.PutObjectInput{
        Bucket: aws.String("my-bucket"),
        Key:    aws.String("hello.txt"),
        Body:   strings.NewReader("Hello from Go!"),
    })

    out, _ := client.ListObjectsV2(ctx, &s3.ListObjectsV2Input{
        Bucket: aws.String("my-bucket"),
    })
    for _, obj := range out.Contents {
        fmt.Printf("%s (%d bytes)\n", *obj.Key, *obj.Size)
    }
}
```


---

# Quickstart - AWS CLI

Source: https://docs.fil.one/quickstart/cli

If you have the AWS CLI installed, you can start using Fil One in under 2 minutes.

```bash
# Install
pip install awscli
# or
brew install awscli

# Configure
aws configure
# Enter your Fil One access key and secret key. Set region to eu-west-1.

# Upload
aws s3 cp my-file.txt s3://my-first-bucket/ --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one

# List
aws s3 ls s3://my-first-bucket/ --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one

# Download
aws s3 cp s3://my-first-bucket/my-file.txt ./downloaded.txt --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

Tip: Set up a named profile to avoid repeating --endpoint-url:

```ini
# ~/.aws/config
[profile filone]
endpoint_url = https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
region = eu-west-1
```

```ini
# ~/.aws/credentials
[filone]
aws_access_key_id = YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
aws_secret_access_key = YOUR_SECRET_KEY
```

Then use `--profile filone` on every command:

```bash
aws s3 ls --profile filone
```


---

# Quickstart - SDK

Source: https://docs.fil.one/quickstart/sdk

Each example uploads a file and verifies it. Create the bucket first in the
dashboard — CreateBucket over the S3 API is not available in eu-west-1, the
default region these examples use.

Note: the endpoint depends on your bucket's region. These examples use
eu-west-1, the default. For a bucket in us-east-1, use
https://us-east-1.s3.fil.one and region us-east-1. The endpoint, the region, and
your access key must all refer to the same region.

## Python

```bash
pip install boto3
```

```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one",
    aws_access_key_id="YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    aws_secret_access_key="YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
    region_name="eu-west-1",
    config=Config(s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
)

# Upload a file (create the bucket first in the dashboard)
s3.upload_file("my-file.txt", "my-sdk-bucket", "my-file.txt")

# Verify
response = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket="my-sdk-bucket")
for obj in response.get("Contents", []):
    print(f"{obj['Key']}  ({obj['Size']} bytes)")
```

## JavaScript

```bash
npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3
```

```javascript
import { S3Client, PutObjectCommand, ListObjectsV2Command } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";
import { readFileSync } from "fs";

const client = new S3Client({
  endpoint: "https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one",
  region: "eu-west-1",
  forcePathStyle: true,
  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY",
    secretAccessKey: "YOUR_SECRET_KEY",
  },
});

// Upload a file (create the bucket first in the dashboard)
await client.send(new PutObjectCommand({
  Bucket: "my-sdk-bucket",
  Key: "my-file.txt",
  Body: readFileSync("my-file.txt"),
}));

// Verify
const { Contents } = await client.send(
  new ListObjectsV2Command({ Bucket: "my-sdk-bucket" })
);
Contents?.forEach((obj) => console.log(obj.Key, obj.Size));
```

## Go

```bash
go get github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3
go get github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials
```

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "strings"

    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/aws"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3"
)

func main() {
    client := s3.New(s3.Options{
        BaseEndpoint:  aws.String("https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one"),
        Region:        "eu-west-1",
        UsePathStyle:  true,
        Credentials: credentials.NewStaticCredentialsProvider(
            os.Getenv("FIL_ACCESS_KEY"),
            os.Getenv("FIL_SECRET_KEY"),
            "",
        ),
    })

    ctx := context.Background()

    // Upload (create the bucket first in the dashboard)
    client.PutObject(ctx, &s3.PutObjectInput{
        Bucket: aws.String("my-sdk-bucket"),
        Key:    aws.String("hello.txt"),
        Body:   strings.NewReader("Hello from Go!"),
    })

    // List
    out, _ := client.ListObjectsV2(ctx, &s3.ListObjectsV2Input{
        Bucket: aws.String("my-sdk-bucket"),
    })
    for _, obj := range out.Contents {
        fmt.Printf("%s (%d bytes)\n", *obj.Key, *obj.Size)
    }
}
```

For more detailed examples including multipart uploads and presigned URLs, see
the dedicated SDK pages for Python, JavaScript, and Go.

# Buckets

Source: https://docs.fil.one/storage/buckets

Buckets are containers for your objects. Every object in Fil One lives inside a bucket.

## Bucket naming rules

- Between 3 and 63 characters
- Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (no dots)
- Must start and end with a letter or number
- Unique within Fil One

These rules are close to AWS S3's but not identical: Fil One does NOT allow dots
(.) in bucket names, which AWS S3 permits. A bucket named `my.data.bucket` must be
renamed when migrating.

## Creating a bucket

Whether you can create or delete a bucket through the S3 API depends on the
region: CreateBucket and DeleteBucket are supported in us-east-1 but not in
eu-west-1, where buckets are created through the Fil One dashboard. All other S3
operations work normally via the API in every region. To use CreateBucket or
DeleteBucket with an access key, grant the key that permission at creation.

1. From the dashboard, click **New bucket**, then **Create bucket**.
2. Enter a bucket name.
3. Choose a region, and optionally enable versioning → Object Lock → retention (all permanent), and create or configure an API key.
4. Click **Create bucket**.

Every bucket is created with encryption enabled automatically.

## Listing buckets

```bash
aws s3 ls --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

```python
response = s3.list_buckets()
for bucket in response["Buckets"]:
    print(bucket["Name"], bucket["CreationDate"])
```

## Deleting a bucket

Deleting a bucket from the dashboard is not yet available. The delete button is
visible but disabled while the underlying storage layer completes support for
this operation, and it will be enabled in a future release.

In the meantime you can delete a bucket through the S3 API in us-east-1, using a
key that has the DeleteBucket permission. The bucket must be empty. DeleteBucket
is not available in eu-west-1.

Note: When you delete a bucket and its objects, the data is immediately removed
from your Fil One account. Because Filecoin stores data in sealed sectors, the
underlying storage may persist for a bounded period until the sector naturally
expires (duration set by the storage layer). That residual data stays encrypted,
and key custody sits with the regional storage operator rather than with you or
Fil One. This does not affect your ability to manage your data in Fil One.


---

# Objects

Source: https://docs.fil.one/storage/objects

Objects are the files you store in Fil One. Each object consists of the file data,
a key (the file path/name), and metadata.

## Uploading objects

```bash
# Upload a single file
aws s3 cp my-file.txt s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one

# Upload a directory
aws s3 sync ./local-folder s3://my-bucket/folder/ \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

```python
# Upload a file
s3.upload_file("my-file.txt", "my-bucket", "my-file.txt")

# Upload with metadata
s3.put_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="report.pdf",
    Body=open("report.pdf", "rb"),
    ContentType="application/pdf",
)
```

For very large objects (above the single-PUT limit — the standard S3 5 GB, not independently confirmed for Fil One), use multipart upload.

## Downloading objects

```bash
aws s3 cp s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt ./my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

```python
s3.download_file("my-bucket", "my-file.txt", "my-file.txt")
```

## Listing objects

```bash
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/ --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

Programmatic listing with pagination:

```python
paginator = s3.get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket="my-bucket"):
    for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
        print(obj["Key"], obj["Size"])
```

## Deleting objects

```bash
aws s3 rm s3://my-bucket/my-file.txt \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```

On a bucket without versioning, deletion is immediate — the object disappears from
the dashboard and API instantly, and there is no recycle bin or soft-delete. On a
versioned bucket a plain delete places a delete marker instead: prior versions are
retained, downloadable by version ID, and still counted as stored storage.

## Presigned URLs

Generate a temporary URL that grants time-limited access to a specific object
without requiring API credentials.

```python
# Generate a download URL valid for 1 hour
url = s3.generate_presigned_url(
    "get_object",
    Params={"Bucket": "my-bucket", "Key": "shared-report.pdf"},
    ExpiresIn=3600,
)
```

Presigned URLs work for both GetObject (downloads) and PutObject (uploads).


---

# Multipart Uploads

Source: https://docs.fil.one/storage/multipart-uploads

For very large objects you must use multipart upload. The single-PUT ceiling is
the standard S3 5 GB, which Fil One's gateway is expected to follow but which is
not independently confirmed. Recommended for any file over 100 MB for improved
reliability. Note: the dashboard uploads with a single PUT, so multipart applies
when using your own SDK/CLI; there is no lifecycle rule to auto-abort incomplete
uploads. The 5 TB / 10,000-part / 5 MB-5 GB part limits are standard S3 values,
not independently confirmed.

## How it works

1. **Initiate** the upload and receive an upload ID.
2. **Upload parts** individually (minimum 5 MB each, except the last part).
3. **Complete** the upload by listing all parts.

## AWS CLI

The AWS CLI handles multipart uploads automatically for large files:

```bash
aws s3 cp large-file.zip s3://my-bucket/large-file.zip \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one

# Configure thresholds
aws configure set s3.multipart_threshold 100MB
aws configure set s3.multipart_chunksize 50MB
```

## Python (boto3)

```python
from boto3.s3.transfer import TransferConfig

config = TransferConfig(
    multipart_threshold=100 * 1024 * 1024,  # 100 MB
    multipart_chunksize=50 * 1024 * 1024,   # 50 MB
    max_concurrency=10,
)

s3.upload_file("large-file.zip", "my-bucket", "large-file.zip", Config=config)
```

## Limits

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Maximum object size | 5 TB |
| Maximum parts | 10,000 |
| Minimum part size | 5 MB (except last part) |
| Maximum part size | 5 GB |

## Cleaning up incomplete uploads

```bash
aws s3api list-multipart-uploads \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one

aws s3api abort-multipart-upload \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key large-file.zip \
  --upload-id YOUR_UPLOAD_ID \
  --endpoint-url https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
```


---

# Versioning

Source: https://docs.fil.one/storage/versioning

Versioning is opt-in and configured at bucket creation time. Once enabled on a
bucket it cannot be suspended or disabled. Every upload to an existing key on a
versioned bucket creates a new version rather than overwriting the previous one,
so any previous state of an object can be retrieved by its version ID.
Versioning is required for Object Lock.

## How versions work

The first upload of `reports/q1.pdf` creates version v1; a later upload of the
same key creates v2 and leaves v1 intact. Deleting the object places a delete
marker at the current version — the object appears deleted, but all previous
versions are still retrievable.

## Billing implications

Every version is a full copy of the object and is billed as stored storage.
Uploading and then overwriting 100 files leaves 200 billable object versions
consuming storage.

## Listing versions

```bash
# List all versions in a bucket
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket my-bucket --profile filone

# List versions for a specific object
aws s3api list-object-versions \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --prefix reports/q1.pdf \
  --profile filone
```

```python
paginator = s3.get_paginator("list_object_versions")
for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket="my-bucket", Prefix="reports/q1.pdf"):
    for version in page.get("Versions", []):
        print(version["VersionId"], version["LastModified"], version["Size"])
    for marker in page.get("DeleteMarkers", []):
        print("DELETE MARKER", marker["VersionId"], marker["LastModified"])
```

## Retrieving a specific version

```bash
aws s3api get-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  q1-old.pdf \
  --profile filone
```

```python
s3.download_file(
    "my-bucket",
    "reports/q1.pdf",
    "q1-old.pdf",
    ExtraArgs={"VersionId": "YOUR_VERSION_ID"},
)
```

## Going back to a previous version

The Fil One dashboard has no restore, roll-back, or "make current" button — you
can list, download, and delete prior versions there, but not promote one to
current.

Note: promoting a version to current with CopyObject is confirmed working in
us-east-1. This has not yet been confirmed in eu-west-1 — use the
download-and-reupload method there instead.

In us-east-1, copy the version onto the current key. Use CopyObject with
x-amz-copy-source-version-id to promote an older version to current in place:

```bash
aws s3api copy-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --copy-source "my-bucket/reports/q1.pdf?versionId=OLD_VERSION_ID" \
  --profile filone
```

```python
s3.copy_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    CopySource={
        "Bucket": "my-bucket",
        "Key": "reports/q1.pdf",
        "VersionId": "OLD_VERSION_ID",
    },
)
```

This creates a new current version with the old content; the version copied from
stays intact.

In eu-west-1, or as a universal fallback, download and re-upload. The re-upload
becomes a new current version, and the version copied from stays intact:

```bash
aws s3api get-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id OLD_VERSION_ID \
  q1-restored.pdf \
  --profile filone

aws s3api put-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --body q1-restored.pdf \
  --profile filone
```

```python
old = s3.get_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    VersionId="OLD_VERSION_ID",
)

s3.put_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    Body=old["Body"].read(),
)
```

If the current version is a delete marker, the object can instead be made
visible again by deleting that delete marker by its version ID.

## Delete markers

Deleting an object without specifying a version ID places a delete marker at the
top of the version stack. The object appears deleted in standard listings and
GetObject returns NoSuchKey. Previous versions remain intact and retrievable by
version ID. To permanently delete a specific version (including a delete
marker), specify the version ID:

```bash
# Delete a specific version permanently
aws s3api delete-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  --profile filone

# Remove a delete marker (restores the object to visible)
aws s3api delete-object \
  --bucket my-bucket \
  --key reports/q1.pdf \
  --version-id DELETE_MARKER_VERSION_ID \
  --profile filone
```

```python
s3.delete_object(
    Bucket="my-bucket",
    Key="reports/q1.pdf",
    VersionId="YOUR_VERSION_ID",
)
```

Note: permanently deleting a version cannot be undone. If the version has an
active Object Lock Compliance retention, the delete request is rejected.

## Versioning and Object Lock

Object Lock is configured on the bucket, when the bucket is created, and
requires versioning on the same bucket. Neither can be turned on later.
Retention is then tracked per version: the bucket's default retention is applied
to each new object version as it is uploaded, and each version carries its own
retention independently. In practice:

- A version under active Compliance retention cannot be deleted, regardless of
  whether a delete marker exists above it.
- A delete marker is not itself protected by retention, so an object can appear
  deleted while its underlying versions remain locked and intact.
- Because retention comes from the bucket default, a bucket with a long default
  retention accumulates locked versions on every overwrite. Each is billed as
  stored storage and cannot be removed until its retention expires.


---

# Object Lock

Source: https://docs.fil.one/storage/object-lock

Object Lock enforces Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) protection. Depending on the
mode, a locked object cannot be deleted or overwritten until its retention
period expires — in Compliance mode, not even by the account owner. Whether it
satisfies a specific regulation is for your own compliance review to decide.

## Key concepts

- Retention period — a duration during which an object version cannot be deleted
  or overwritten.
- Compliance mode — the strictest protection. No user, including the account
  owner, can shorten the retention period or delete a locked object before it
  expires.
- Governance mode — a softer protection. In standard S3, a caller holding a
  special bypass permission can override Governance retention and delete objects
  early. Fil One does NOT currently expose a grantable bypass permission, so in
  practice a Governance-locked object is protected for its retention period the
  same way a Compliance one is; the difference is that Governance is not
  positioned as an absolute, unbypassable guarantee at the platform level.
- Versioning — Object Lock requires versioning, so both are enabled when
  creating the bucket. Versioning cannot be suspended once set.

## Enabling Object Lock

Object Lock is opt-in and must be enabled at bucket creation time. It cannot be
added to an existing bucket, and once enabled it cannot be disabled.

1. From the dashboard, click **New bucket**, then **Create bucket**.
2. Enter a bucket name.
3. Enable **Versioning**.
4. Enable **Object Lock**.
5. Select a retention mode: **Governance** (the default) or **Compliance**.
6. Set a default retention duration — from 1 day up to 100 years (36,500 days).
7. Click **Create bucket**.

## Retention modes

| Mode | Can it be overridden early? | Typical use |
|------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| Governance (default) | Not through any Fil One-granted permission today | Internal-policy retention, audit-friendly workflows |
| Compliance | No — not by anyone, including account owners | Strict, long-term immutable record-keeping |

In Compliance mode the retention period is absolute; no action can shorten or
remove it once set. In Governance mode, standard S3 allows a caller with the
bypass permission to delete locked objects early, but Fil One does not currently
expose that permission, so today a Governance lock behaves like a firm retention
lock rather than a routinely-overridable one.

Note: choose the retention mode carefully at bucket creation — it is fixed for
the life of the bucket. There is no update-bucket operation, so a Governance
bucket cannot be converted into a Compliance one later, or objects migrated
between them without a full download and re-upload. Compliance retention
periods, once set, cannot be shortened or removed.

## Setting per-object retention

The default retention period set at bucket creation is applied automatically to
every object uploaded to that bucket.

Note: PutObjectRetention is region-dependent. Setting or changing retention on
an individual object version via PutObjectRetention is offered as a grantable
access-key permission. It is confirmed working in us-east-1 — including
extending a retention period and, using the standard S3
bypass-governance-retention mechanism, shortening one (a protocol-level
capability of the gateway, NOT a permission Fil One's own access keys can
grant). It has not yet been confirmed in eu-west-1 — until then, rely on the
bucket-level default set at creation for guaranteed retention there.

Object Lock buckets are always versioned, so a retention call should target a
specific version with --version-id; without it the call targets whatever the
current version is (possibly a delete marker).

```bash
aws s3api put-object-retention \
  --bucket my-compliance-bucket \
  --key important-record.pdf \
  --version-id YOUR_VERSION_ID \
  --retention '{"Mode": "COMPLIANCE", "RetainUntilDate": "2027-12-31T00:00:00Z"}' \
  --endpoint-url https://us-east-1.s3.fil.one
```

```python
s3.put_object_retention(
    Bucket="my-compliance-bucket",
    Key="important-record.pdf",
    VersionId="YOUR_VERSION_ID",
    Retention={
        "Mode": "COMPLIANCE",
        "RetainUntilDate": "2027-12-31T00:00:00Z",
    },
)
```

In standard S3, retention can be extended but never shortened: RetainUntilDate
can move further into the future but not closer, and shortening a Compliance
retention period is rejected with 403 AccessDenied. Fil One's us-east-1 gateway
has been confirmed to follow this; eu-west-1 has not yet been independently
verified.

## Checking retention status

The object detail page in the dashboard shows an object's retention status and
displays a lock banner for Compliance-locked objects. GetObjectRetention is also
available over the S3 API:

```bash
aws s3api get-object-retention \
  --bucket my-compliance-bucket \
  --key important-record.pdf \
  --endpoint-url https://us-east-1.s3.fil.one
```

## Deleting locked objects

Attempting to delete an object with active retention returns 403 AccessDenied.
On a versioned bucket, a DELETE without a version ID places a delete marker: the
object appears deleted to applications, but the underlying version remains
protected and intact until retention expires.

## Deleting buckets with locked objects

Bucket deletion is currently restricted regardless of retention state. The
dashboard delete button is disabled while the underlying storage layer completes
support for this operation, and over the S3 API DeleteBucket is only available in
us-east-1 (not eu-west-1). Active Compliance retention is one more reason a
bucket cannot be removed, but it is not the only one — do not assume a bucket
becomes freely deletable simply because its retention periods have expired.

## Object Lock and API keys

GetBucketVersioning and GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration are selectable
permissions granted when creating a key — they are not included automatically.
Beyond that:

- A key with Delete permission can delete objects in Governance mode buckets
  once retention has expired. Fil One does not expose a bypass permission for
  deleting before expiry.
- Compliance mode cannot be overridden by any key, regardless of permissions.
- To set retention on an individual version, grant the PutObjectRetention
  granular permission — available in BOTH REGIONS, never granted automatically.

## Object Lock during trial

Object Lock is fully available during the free trial, with no trial-specific
retention cap. Trial and paid accounts alike can set retention from 1 day to 100
years (36,500 days).

Note: a trial lock cannot be undone. Retention outlives the trial — a lock set
during the trial still applies after it ends, and Compliance retention cannot be
shortened once set. Because durations run up to 100 years, an object
Compliance-locked while testing keeps occupying storage (and generating storage
cost once on a paid plan) for the entire retention period, with no way to delete
it early. Use short durations while evaluating.

## Object Lock and the Filecoin storage model

When an object is deleted after its retention period expires, it is immediately
removed from the Fil One account and inaccessible via the API and dashboard.
Because Filecoin stores data in sealed sectors, the underlying storage may
persist for a bounded period until the sector naturally expires; the exact
duration is set by the storage layer rather than measured by Fil One. That
residual data stays encrypted, and key custody sits with the regional storage
operator rather than with the customer or Fil One.

## Common use cases

Object Lock provides WORM-style retention. These describe the use case, not a
claim that Fil One is certified for the named regulation:

| Use case | Typical retention | What Object Lock provides |
|----------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| Financial records | 6-7 years | Immutable, non-rewritable storage for the retention period |
| Healthcare records | 6-10 years | Prevents deletion or overwrite of records under retention |
| Ransomware-resistant backup | 30-90 days | Backups cannot be encrypted-over or deleted while locked |
| Legal preservation | Variable | Retention-based preservation of evidence, or S3 Legal Hold |
| Audit-log retention | Varies | Keeps logs unmodified for a fixed window |

## On regulatory compliance

Object Lock provides WORM-style retention, a building block many regulatory
regimes call for. However:

- Fil One holds NO third-party compliance attestation (for example, an SEC
  17a-4 assessment) for this feature.
- Retention enforcement at the storage gateway is confirmed in us-east-1 and NOT
  yet independently verified in eu-west-1.
- The product surfaces NO per-object cryptographic proof (no CID, deal ID, or
  seal state) that could be presented to an auditor to demonstrate integrity.

Treat the regulations named above as illustrative use cases, and evaluate
whether Object Lock meets a specific obligation as part of your own compliance
process.


---

# Account Security

Source: https://docs.fil.one/security/account-security

Covers securing the account you sign in with. API request authentication is a
separate mechanism (see Authentication / API Keys).

## Signing in

Four methods: passkeys (the primary method), Google, GitHub, and email with
password. A new account must verify its email address before the dashboard
opens; until then every page redirects to a verification screen.

## Two-factor authentication

Opt-in per user, managed from Settings > Security. Three factor types:

| Factor | Dashboard label | What it is |
|--------|-----------------|------------|
| Authenticator app | Authenticator app (OTP) | Time-based one-time code from an app (1Password, Authy, Google Authenticator) |
| Security key | Security key | Roaming WebAuthn authenticator, e.g. a YubiKey |
| Device biometrics | Device biometrics | Platform WebAuthn authenticator: Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello |

SMS and email codes are DELIBERATELY NOT OFFERED (SIM-swap and
mailbox-compromise risk). Only device- or app-bound factors are supported. More
than one factor can be enrolled, and individual ones removed.

## Passkeys

Listed separately from two-factor methods, under Settings > Passkeys. With none
enrolled, the dashboard prompts to add one on next sign-in. Limit is 20 passkeys
per account.

## Recovery codes

A single-use code for signing in after losing access to an authenticator.
Generate or replace from Settings > Security > Recovery code > Regenerate.
Generating a new code invalidates the previous one.

## Step-up re-authentication

Four actions require a fresh two-factor check even within a signed-in session:
removing a two-factor method, removing all two-factor methods, removing a
passkey, and regenerating a recovery code. A session not established with a
strong factor is sent back through sign-in first, so someone with access to an
open session cannot quietly strip the account's protections.

## Changing your password

Settings > Security > Password > Change sends a password-reset email to the
registered address.


---

# Authentication

Source: https://docs.fil.one/security/authentication

All API requests to Fil One must be authenticated using AWS Signature Version 4
(SigV4). Any S3-compatible SDK or tool handles this automatically.

## API keys

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Access Key ID | Identifies your account. Included in request headers. Format: FHXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX |
| Secret Access Key | Signs your requests. Never sent over the wire. |

Your secret key is displayed once at creation time. If you lose it, you must
create a new key pair.

## Configuring your client

### AWS CLI

```bash
aws configure
# AWS Access Key ID: YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
# AWS Secret Access Key: YOUR_SECRET_KEY
# Default region name: eu-west-1
```

Named profile (recommended):

```ini
# ~/.aws/config  (AWS CLI v2 — v1 ignores endpoint_url)
[profile filone]
endpoint_url = https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one
region = eu-west-1
s3 =
    addressing_style = path

# ~/.aws/credentials
[filone]
aws_access_key_id = YOUR_ACCESS_KEY
aws_secret_access_key = YOUR_SECRET_KEY
```

### Python (boto3)

```python
import boto3
import os
from botocore.config import Config

s3 = boto3.client(
    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one",
    aws_access_key_id=os.environ["FIL_ACCESS_KEY"],
    aws_secret_access_key=os.environ["FIL_SECRET_KEY"],
    region_name="eu-west-1",
    config=Config(s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),  # required
)
```

### JavaScript (AWS SDK v3)

```javascript
import { S3Client } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3";

const client = new S3Client({
  endpoint: "https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one",
  region: "eu-west-1",
  forcePathStyle: true,
  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: process.env.FIL_ACCESS_KEY,
    secretAccessKey: process.env.FIL_SECRET_KEY,
  },
});
```

### Go

```go
func newClient() *s3.Client {
    return s3.New(s3.Options{
        BaseEndpoint: aws.String("https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one"),
        Region:       "eu-west-1",
        UsePathStyle: true,
        Credentials: credentials.NewStaticCredentialsProvider(
            os.Getenv("FIL_ACCESS_KEY"),
            os.Getenv("FIL_SECRET_KEY"),
            "",
        ),
    })
}
```

## Security best practices

- Do not hardcode credentials in source code. Use environment variables or a
  secrets manager.
- Create separate keys for different environments.
- Rotate keys periodically.
- Revoke keys immediately if compromised.


---

# API Keys

Source: https://docs.fil.one/security/api-keys

API keys authenticate your requests to the Fil One S3 API. Each key consists of
an Access Key ID (public identifier) and a Secret Access Key (used to sign requests).

## Creating an API key

1. Go to **API Keys** in the left menu of the dashboard.
2. Click **Create new key** (opens a dedicated page).
3. Give the key a descriptive name (e.g., production-backend, ci-pipeline). Max 64 chars.
4. Choose the key's region (required, fixed) and set permissions and bucket scope. At least one permission is required.
5. Optionally set an expiration: Never, 30 days, or a Custom date.
6. Click **Create key**.
7. **Copy the Secret Access Key immediately.** It is shown only once.

## Key permissions

| Permission | What it allows |
|------------|----------------|
| Read | GetObject (and HeadObject, same underlying permission), ListMultipartUploadParts |
| Write | PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload |
| List | ListObjectsV2 / ListBucket, ListBucketMultipartUploads |
| Delete | DeleteObject |

Listing your bucket names (ListAllMyBuckets) is granted to every key automatically and is not one of the permissions above. Governance Object Lock has no grantable bypass permission in the product. PutObjectRetention and Legal Hold (GetObjectLegalHold/PutObjectLegalHold) are grantable and confirmed working in us-east-1; neither has yet been verified in eu-west-1. The key list in the dashboard has no Region column — record each key's region yourself.

## Bucket scope

By default, a key has access to all buckets in your account. You can restrict a
key to specific buckets. This limits the blast radius of a compromised key.

## Key expiration

You can set an expiration date when creating a key. After expiration, the key no
longer authenticates and requests fail with a 403 (typically AccessDenied or
InvalidAccessKeyId). Revocation/deletion is forwarded to the regional operator;
treat it as effective quickly rather than at a guaranteed instant.

## Security best practices

- Use separate keys per environment (development, staging, production).
- Use the minimum permissions required.
- Scope keys to specific buckets when possible.
- Set expiration dates on temporary keys.
- Rotate keys periodically.
- Revoke immediately if compromised.
- Never hardcode credentials in source code.


---

# Encryption

Source: https://docs.fil.one/security/encryption

Fil One encrypts all data by default. There is nothing to configure.

## Encryption at rest

All objects are encrypted at rest. Applied automatically on write, decrypted
automatically on read, and it cannot be disabled. Applies to all objects in all
buckets with no exceptions. Encryption is performed by the S3 storage gateway for
the bucket's region, not by the Fil One console. The specific cipher is set by the
regional operator and is not documented here.

## Encryption in transit

All connections to the regional endpoints (https://eu-west-1.s3.fil.one,
https://us-east-1.s3.fil.one) use TLS. HTTP connections are rejected.
Applies to all API operations including uploads, downloads, presigned URLs,
and metadata requests.

## Client-side encryption

Optional. If your requirements call for client-side encryption, encrypt the bytes
in your own application before uploading. AWS's S3 Encryption Client exists only
for some SDKs (Java, .NET, Go, Ruby) — NOT boto3, the AWS CLI, or JS v3 — so with
those you supply your own crypto. Fil One stores whatever bytes you send.
Client-side encryption is in addition to the server-side encryption that Fil One
applies automatically.


---

# Certifications & Trust

Source: https://docs.fil.one/security/certifications-and-trust

Certification status and security posture. NOT the Object Lock "Compliance"
retention mode, which is a separate feature (see Object Lock).

## Certification status

SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are actively being pursued. Fil One does not hold
either certification today, and holds no third-party compliance attestation for
any feature, including the SEC 17a-4 assessments often asked about for WORM
retention workloads. Contact security@fil.one for where that work stands.

## Controls in place today

| Area | What is in place |
|------|------------------|
| Authentication | Passkeys (primary method), Google, GitHub, email with password. |
| Multi-factor | Opt-in per user: authenticator apps (TOTP), WebAuthn security keys, device biometrics. SMS deliberately not offered. |
| Access control | Access keys scoped to a single region and to specific permissions (Read, Write, List, Delete), optionally restricted to named buckets, with optional expiry. |
| Encryption | Always on, at rest and in transit. TLS enforced, HTTP rejected, cannot be disabled. |
| Retention (WORM) | Object Lock in Governance and Compliance modes, 1 day to 100 years. A Compliance-mode lock binds every caller including the account owner. |

## Demonstrating a control is in force

Auditors want evidence, not a statement that a feature exists. Producible by the
customer today:

| To show | Call | Returns |
|---------|------|---------|
| An object version is under retention | GetObjectRetention | Mode (GOVERNANCE/COMPLIANCE) and RetainUntilDate |
| A bucket's default retention policy | GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration | Mode and duration applied to new versions |
| A legal hold is active | GetObjectLegalHold | Hold status |
| Versioning is enabled | GetBucketVersioning | Enabled |

GetObjectRetention and GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration work in both regions.
GetObjectLegalHold is confirmed in us-east-1, not yet confirmed in eu-west-1.
These reads need the matching access-key permissions, which are selectable at
key creation rather than granted by default. A failed delete is also evidence:
deleting an object under active retention returns 403 AccessDenied, reproducible
on demand. What CANNOT be produced is a per-object cryptographic artefact.

## Shared responsibility

| Layer | Operated by | Responsible for |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|
| Console, API, identity, billing | Fil One | Authentication, access-key issuance and scoping, multi-factor enrolment, dashboard, request authorization, subscription state |
| Regional S3 storage gateway | Regional storage operator | Serving object data, applying server-side encryption at rest, custody of encryption keys |
| Underlying storage network | Filecoin storage providers | Holding data and producing the network's proof-of-storage |

Practical consequence: encryption at rest is applied and keyed by the regional
storage operator, so there is no customer-managed-key or SSE-C option and the
cipher in use is set by that operator. Questions turning on the exact scheme or
on key custody for a region go to support, who route them to the operator.

## Who to ask

Fil One's own controls (authentication, access keys, the console):
security@fil.one. The storage gateway's encryption implementation or key
custody: contact support, who route to the regional operator.

## Scope of what Fil One claims

- Proof-of-storage is a NETWORK property. Filecoin providers continuously prove
  they still hold committed data, but Fil One does not surface per-object content
  identifiers, deal IDs, or seal state, so there is no per-object artefact to
  hand an auditor.
- Named regulations describe USE CASES, not certifications. Where these docs
  mention SEC 17a-4, FINRA, HIPAA or similar, they describe a scenario the
  underlying capability supports. Whether a feature satisfies a specific
  obligation is a determination for your own compliance review.

---

# Pricing

Source: https://docs.fil.one/billing/pricing

Fil One is priced at **$4.99 / TB / month**, with a **$4.99 / month minimum**. If you store less than 1 TB, you are billed the $4.99 minimum.

No egress fees, no per-request charges, no hidden costs.

## How billing is calculated

Your bill is based on the average amount of data you store over the billing period. Stored bytes are sampled by a metering job that runs twice a day (~07:00 and 19:00 UTC) and averaged. Storage is charged at a single flat rate of $4.99 per TB per month with a $4.99/month minimum — there is no separate "first TB" tier, just one linear rate plus a floor. Storage is measured in decimal units (1 TB = 1,000 GB).

Illustrative figures (steady amount stored for the full month, at $4.99/TB with the $4.99 minimum applied): 500 GB ≈ $4.99 (minimum applies); 1 TB (1,000 GB) ≈ $4.99; 1.5 TB ≈ $7.49; 2 TB ≈ $9.98. These are illustrative — your invoice on the Billing page is the source of truth for exact amounts. Storage that changes during the month is averaged first.


---

# Trial & Billing

Source: https://docs.fil.one/billing/trial

## Free trial

Every new account starts with a 30-day free trial. No credit card required.

| Included | Amount |
|----------|--------|
| Storage | 1 TB (1,000 GB) |
| Egress bandwidth | 2 TB (cumulative over the trial) |
| API operations | Unlimited |
| Duration | 30 days from account creation |

The two caps are enforcement thresholds, not soft allowances, and behave differently: reaching the storage cap (1 TB) WRITE-LOCKS the account (reads still work), while reaching the egress cap (2 TB) DISABLES it entirely (no access), the same state as trial expiry. Trial egress is a single cumulative budget for the whole 30 days, not a monthly amount that resets. Enforcement runs on a twice-daily usage job (~07:00/19:00 UTC), so a cap can be exceeded for a few hours before access changes. Generating shareable links and viewing invoice history are the two features reserved for paid plans.

## What happens when the trial ends

| Phase | Days | What you can do |
|-------|------|-----------------|
| Active trial | 0-30 | Full access. |
| Grace period | 31-37 | Read-only. Download your data and upgrade. |
| Expired | 38+ | Account disabled. No access to data, uploads, or API keys. |

You can upgrade to a paid plan at any time during the trial or grace period. Disabling blocks all access to the account; Fil One does not run an automatic purge at that point, so contact support to restore access or request removal of your data.

## Paid plan pricing

| Component | Price |
|-----------|-------|
| Storage | $4.99 / TB / month |
| Egress bandwidth | No charge |
| API operations | Included |

Billed on average daily usage, with a $4.99 / month minimum. If you store less than 1 TB, you are billed the $4.99 minimum. No contract or term commitment. If a payment fails, the account enters **past due** and writes are blocked immediately (reads continue); the ~30-day past-due window is retrieval-only before the account is disabled. Cancellation is done through the Stripe billing portal, and the 30-day grace period starts when Stripe actually cancels the subscription.


---

# Usage

Source: https://docs.fil.one/billing/usage

The Billing page in the dashboard shows current usage for the active billing
period.

## What is measured

| Metric | How it's measured |
|--------|------------------|
| Storage | Average daily storage across the billing period, in GB or TB |
| Egress bandwidth | Total data downloaded from Fil One in the billing period |

Storage is measured as an average rather than a peak — storing 2 TB for half the
month and 1 TB for the other half bills 1.5 TB. Fil One counts storage in
decimal units: 1 TB is 1,000 GB, and 1 GB is 1,000,000,000 bytes.

On a paid plan, egress is NOT charged — there are no egress fees. During the
trial, egress is capped.

## Trial limits

During the free trial, usage is capped at:

- Storage — 1 TB (1,000 GB): reaching this limit WRITE-LOCKS the account. Reads
  and downloads still work; new uploads are rejected.
- Egress — 2 TB (2,000 GB), cumulative over the whole trial: reaching this limit
  DISABLES the account entirely — no read or write access — the same state as
  trial expiry. This is a single budget for the full 30 days, not a monthly
  amount that resets.

These caps are enforced by a usage job that runs twice a day (around 07:00 and
19:00 UTC), so a cap may be exceeded for a few hours before the account state
changes — there is no real-time block at the exact moment it is crossed.
Upgrading to a paid plan removes both caps immediately.

## Versioning and storage costs

If versioning is enabled on a bucket, every version of an object counts as
stored storage. Overwriting a 1 GB file 10 times results in 10 GB of stored
versions.

## Billing period

Paid accounts are billed monthly. The billing period resets on the same day each
month (the date of the first upgrade from trial). Usage resets at the start of
each new billing period.


---

# App: Dashboard

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/dashboard

The console home page, reached from "Dashboard" at the top of the left sidebar.
Sign-in, email verification, MFA and passkeys are covered on Account Security.

## Quick setup

Until all three are done, a "QUICK SETUP" card tracks progress as "n of 3":
Create a bucket, Upload an object, Generate API key. It disappears when complete.

## Plan, storage and egress cards

- PLAN: plan name plus status badge (Active / Past Due / Grace Period /
  Canceled / No plan). On trial the badge counts down "n days left" and hovering
  shows the exact expiry. Footer link goes to Billing.
- STORAGE: usage; on trial adds "/ 1 TB" and a progress bar, on paid shows an
  "Est. monthly cost" row instead.
- EGRESS: usage; on trial adds "/ 2 TB" and a progress bar, on paid reads
  "No egress fees · unlimited".
- A strip below shows BUCKETS / OBJECTS / API KEYS totals, with "View all" links
  for buckets and API keys.

How to read the numbers:
- SIZES ARE DECIMAL. 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes, 1 TB = 1,000 GB.
- STORAGE IS A PERIODIC POINT-IN-TIME READING, not live, so a very recent upload
  or delete may not be reflected yet.
- EGRESS IS A ROLLING 30-DAY TOTAL, not a calendar month, so it does not reset on
  the 1st.
- "Est. monthly cost" applies $4.99/TB to the latest storage reading, with the
  account's monthly minimum as the floor. THE INVOICE IS CALCULATED FROM AVERAGE
  STORAGE over the month, so the two figures differ. The estimate excludes egress
  (free on paid plans).

## Usage Trends

Charts a 7-day (default) or 30-day window: storage as an area chart, objects as a
bar chart. Each point is a daily reading, and days without a reading are plotted
as zero, so a data gap appears as a dip to zero.

NOTE: the figure above the OBJECTS chart is the SUM of the daily readings across
the window, so it runs higher than the current object count. The OBJECTS total in
the summary strip is the current count; the chart shows the trend.

## Recent Activity

The five most recent events with relative timestamps ("5m ago", "2d ago").
The feed currently covers bucket-created and key-created events, shown as
"bucket created" and "key created". OBJECT-LEVEL EVENTS ARE NOT INCLUDED YET, so
confirm an upload by opening the bucket rather than by reading this feed. Empty
state: "No activity yet" plus a "Create bucket" button.

## Account state banners (app-wide, not just the dashboard)

- Trial storage cap reached: "Storage limit exceeded. Uploads are disabled.
  Delete files or upgrade to resume."
- Trial expired, in grace: says the trial expired with days left to upgrade or
  download data.
- Account disabled: "Account disabled. Visit billing to restore access."

Reads keep working while writes are paused, so data stays available to download.


---

# App: Buckets

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/buckets

Console-specific. Concepts, S3 equivalents and code samples live on Buckets,
Objects, Versioning and Object Lock.

## Bucket list

Columns: Name, Region (label plus region id), Created, Visibility, Features
(Versioned / Object Lock badges). All buckets are listed together in API order;
there is no search, filter or sort control. Empty state: "No buckets yet" plus
"Create bucket".

BUCKET DELETION RUNS THROUGH THE S3 API, NOT THE CONSOLE: the per-row trash icon
is disabled with tooltip "Deleting buckets is not available yet". Over the API it
works in us-east-1 (bucket must be empty); DeleteBucket is unavailable in
eu-west-1.

## Creating a bucket

1. Bucket name: 3-63 chars, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens, must start and end
   alphanumeric, NO DOTS (unlike AWS S3), globally unique.
2. Region: eu-west-1 Europe (France) default, or us-east-1 US East (Michigan).
3. Object settings, three switches nested in order, ALL OFF BY DEFAULT:
   Versioning, then Object Lock (available once Versioning is on), then Retention
   (available once Object Lock is on). Turning a parent off resets what nests
   inside it. Retention reveals a "Default Retention Policy": Governance
   (default) or Compliance, plus a "Lock period" in Days or Years, DEFAULT 15
   DAYS, maximum 100 years.

An optional "Create new key" section creates an access key alongside the bucket,
pre-scoped to that bucket and region; the submit button becomes "Create bucket
and API key" and the secret is shown once in a dialog.

An "Included by default" panel states: all data encrypted at rest, and every
bucket private (access requires an API key).

PERMANENT AT CREATION: name, region, versioning, Object Lock and default
retention, in the console and over the API alike (no update-bucket operation).
Create a new bucket for a different configuration.

## Inside a bucket

Header shows region, storage used, creation time. Property cards: Versioning,
Object Lock, Encryption (always "Enabled"), and Default Retention when set.
Tabs: "Objects (N)" and "API Keys (N)". The API Keys tab includes an "Access
endpoints" block with copyable S3 Endpoint, S3 Path and Region.

Object table columns: Name, Size, Last Modified, plus Version and Status when
versioning is on. Keys containing "/" group into clickable folder rows with a
breadcrumb. On versioned buckets a key with >1 version gets an expander and an
"n versions" pill; badges are "Latest" and "Delete marker". Per-row icon buttons
download or delete one object at a time; there are no bulk/multi-select actions.

LARGE BUCKETS: the browser shows the FIRST PAGE of results (~1,000 entries). The
"Objects (N)" tab count comes from bucket analytics and stays accurate, so on a
large bucket that count is higher than the rows in view. Page through a full
listing with the CLI or an SDK.

## Uploading

"Upload object" on the bucket. Drag files OR whole folders, or use "Select files"
/ "Select folder".

Prefix behaviour: the optional "Prefix" field appears when INDIVIDUAL FILES are
selected. Folder-selected files keep their own relative paths, which take the
place of the prefix. The prefix starts empty each time rather than carrying over
from the folder being browsed.

Selecting files does not upload them; click "Upload n file(s)". A failure gives a
"Retry n failed" button that retries only those files.

SINGLE-PUT, NOT MULTIPART: one request per file, capped by the S3 5 GB single-PUT
ceiling. Use the CLI or an SDK with multipart support above that.

## Object detail page

Shows Name, Size, Bucket, S3 Path, ETag, and where applicable Version ID,
Retention, Description and Tags. Compliance-mode retention adds a "Compliance
retention lock" notice with the date before which deletion is not permitted.

A "Version history" card appears when the object has more than one version,
listing Version ID / Status / Size / Last Modified and marking the one in view.
It is populated from the object listing already fetched, so arrive via the
bucket's object list rather than a direct object link to see it.

NO RESTORE / PROMOTE / MAKE-CURRENT ACTION: to make an earlier version current,
download it and upload it again.

## Downloading and sharing

Download works on any plan INCLUDING TRIAL, from the row or the detail header.

"Share object" generates a link needing no API key, with expiry options 1 hour /
24 hours (default) / 3 days / 7 days, then "Generate link". SHARING IS A
PAID-PLAN FEATURE: on trial the button is disabled with an upgrade tooltip.

## Deleting objects

Trash icon on a row, or "Delete object" on the detail page, then confirm. ONE
OBJECT AT A TIME. Permanent on non-versioned buckets. On versioned buckets a
plain delete writes a delete marker and prior versions are retained and still
billed; deleting a specific version removes only that version.

An object under active retention or a legal hold is protected, and a delete
attempt returns that protection as an error. While an account is past due or in a
grace period, access is read-only and writes resume once payment succeeds.


---

# App: API Keys

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/api-keys

Console-specific. Permission meanings, signing and security guidance live on API
Keys and Authentication.

## Key list

Tabs "API keys" and "Connection details". Columns: Name (with Access Key ID and a
copy button), Buckets ("All Buckets" or per-bucket badges), Permissions (badges,
with finer-grained ones grouped as "Data protection" / "Bucket management" /
"Bucket info"), Status, Last Used. Empty state: "No API keys yet" plus "Create
your first key".

PLACEHOLDER COLUMNS: "Last Used" reads "Never" and "Status" reads "Active" for
every key, and the expiry date set at creation is not shown in this list. Do not
infer from these columns whether a key is in use or still valid; advise keeping
an external record and using descriptive key names.

## Creating a key

Dedicated page via "Create new key".

- Key name: up to 64 chars, letters/numbers/spaces/underscores/hyphens/periods,
  unique within a region.
- Region: REQUIRED. A key is scoped to its region, and each region has its own
  endpoint, so endpoint + region + key must agree. Storing in both regions needs
  one key per region.
- Object permissions: Read (download/retrieve), Write (upload/overwrite), List
  (browse/list), Delete (permanently remove). READ, WRITE AND LIST ARE
  PRE-SELECTED; DELETE IS NOT.
- Finer-grained permissions nest under a checked parent and are granted
  INDIVIDUALLY: under Read = Read object versions, Read retention settings, Read
  legal hold status; under Write = Set retention, Set legal hold; under List =
  List object versions; under Delete = Delete object versions. A key with Write
  therefore also needs "Set retention" ticked before it can apply a retention
  policy. Unchecking a parent clears what nested under it.
- Bucket management: "List all buckets" is always on. "Read bucket versioning"
  and "Read object lock configuration" are available in every region and are
  PRE-SELECTED. "Create bucket" / "Delete bucket" are available only in regions
  supporting bucket management over the S3 API; in eu-west-1 they are disabled
  with tooltip "Not supported in Europe (France)", where buckets are created in
  the console instead.
- Bucket scope: "All buckets" (default, meaning all buckets in the key's region)
  or "Specific buckets", listed filtered to the selected region.
- Expiration: "Never expires" (default), "30 days", or "Custom" date. Enforced by
  the storage layer.

## The secret

A "Save your credentials" dialog shows the Access Key ID and the Secret Access
Key (masked until revealed), with copy buttons and .csv / .env downloads.
FIL ONE NEVER STORES THE SECRET, which is why it appears only at creation and
cannot be retrieved later. Lose it and the key is deleted and replaced.

## Revoking

Row "⋯" menu, then "Delete": the key is permanently revoked and applications
using it lose access immediately. Deletion IS the revocation; to rotate, create
the replacement, migrate, then delete the old key. Revocation is confirmed with
the storage operator BEFORE the key leaves the list, so a listed key is a live
key and the list stays a truthful picture of access.

A bucket's "API Keys" tab lists the keys that can reach that one bucket.

## Bucket Intelligence keys are separate

Keys for querying an indexed bucket are a different credential, not managed here:
bearer tokens that authorize only the query endpoint and cannot read or write
bucket contents.


---

# App: Bucket Intelligence

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/bucket-intelligence

Console-specific, under the "AI Tools" sidebar group. Indexing mechanics, file
types, models and the query API live on Bucket Intelligence.

EARLY ACCESS, ENABLED PER ACCOUNT. Without access the menu item opens a "Coming
Soon" page describing the feature plus a "Join the waitlist" form (use case,
timeline, team size). The nav item itself is always visible.

## Overview strip and tabs

Three tiles: "Files indexed" (with the bucket count they span), "Index size",
"API keys". A tile reads "Unavailable" if the figures fail to load, which does
not affect indexing or querying. Two tabs: "Buckets" and "API Keys".

## Indexing a bucket

Per-row "Index" button (label becomes "Starting…" in flight), then a confirm
dialog stating "Ready in" up to 6 hours (scheduled, NOT on upload) and what is
indexed (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Markdown, HTML, plain text; other files skipped
and left untouched). Confirm with "Start indexing".

To stop: the bucket's actions menu, "Stop indexing". FILES AND THE EXISTING INDEX
ARE KEPT, so indexing can be started again later.

Five status states:

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Not indexed | Indexing not turned on for this bucket |
| Indexing | First pass running; row adds "Up to 6 hours until the first results" |
| Indexing | Later pass running, checking for new and changed files |
| Failed | Last run did not complete; the row shows the reason |
| Ready | Queryable, with file count, index size and last sync time |

A FAILED RUN DOES NOT TURN INDEXING OFF or discard what is already indexed; the
next scheduled pass picks the bucket up again and the console keeps refreshing.

## Asking a question

A "Ready" bucket's button reads "Ask questions" and opens a panel with an "Ask a
question" box. Before the first pass it reads "View details" and the box is
DISABLED, with a note that questions become available after the first pass.

Answers list the objects they drew on, each linking to that object. ONE BUCKET
PER QUERY; query each bucket in turn to cover several.

A "Query from code" block in the same panel holds a ready-made curl call with the
bucket and region already filled in; create a key and export it as
FILONE_RAG_KEY.

## API keys tab

Bearer tokens that authorize the QUERY ENDPOINT ONLY and cannot read or write
bucket contents; separate from S3 access keys. "Create API key" takes a "Name"
and a "Scope" of "All buckets" or "Specific buckets", where the bucket list
offers ALREADY-INDEXED buckets only (index one first if it is empty).

The token appears once in a "Save your API key" dialog (only a hash is stored),
with copy, "Download .env" and "Download .csv". Table columns: Name, Prefix,
Scope, Created, Last used. Deleting takes effect immediately.

"LAST USED" COUNTS KEY CALLS ONLY. Asking questions in the console uses the
signed-in session rather than a key, so console exploration does not move it.

## Reference block

Below the keys table: the query endpoint with placeholders, the models in use
(Titan Text Embeddings V2 for indexing, Claude Opus 4.8 for answers, both marked
"Managed"), and a link to these docs. Bring-your-own-model is marked coming soon.

# App: AI Agent Toolkit

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/ai-agent-toolkit

Under the "AI Tools" sidebar group, next to Bucket Intelligence.

NOT RELEASED. The page is marked "Coming Soon": it introduces what the toolkit
will offer and collects waitlist interest, so THERE IS NOTHING TO SET UP on it
yet. Stated as free during early access, with standard storage rates on the data
itself.

Waitlist form: which tools you are connecting (Claude, Cursor, Continue, ChatGPT,
Zapier, n8n, Make.com, or your own answer), timeline, team size, notes.

## Connecting AI tools today (this part is real)

The toolkit is NOT required to use Fil One from an AI application. Fil One is
S3-compatible, so anything that speaks S3 works now with an ordinary access key:
create a key scoped to the buckets the application should reach, then point the
tool at the region's endpoint with path-style addressing. Frameworks that read
and write object storage directly (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, CrewAI)
connect this way, and a single-bucket key keeps an agent in its own workspace.

For question-answering over a bucket's contents, that exists today as Bucket
Intelligence, a separate early-access feature with its own query API.

Treat the access-key route above as the supported way to connect AI tools today.

# App: Billing

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/billing

Console-specific. Trial lifecycle, pricing model and measurement live on Trial &
Billing, Pricing and Usage.

## Plan card

| Status | Badge | Card text |
|--------|-------|-----------|
| Trial | Active | "Free Trial", days remaining, 1 TB included |
| Paid | Active | "Pay-as-you-go", billed for what you use, monthly minimum in brackets |
| Payment failed | Active | "Pay-as-you-go"; the notice is in the top banner |
| Grace period | Grace Period | "Read-only access", days remaining |
| Canceled | Canceled | "Subscription inactive" |
| No plan | No plan | "Choose a plan to start storing data" |

A FAILED PAYMENT APPEARS IN THE TOP BANNER, NOT THE BADGE, which continues to
read "Active". The account becomes READ-ONLY from the moment payment fails, so
writes stop; they resume once payment succeeds.

Button is "Upgrade" on trial, "Manage plan" on paid, "Reactivate" once lapsed.

## Current usage

"Storage used" always shows; against the 1 TB cap with a progress bar on trial,
figure alone on paid (no cap). "Egress used" is shown against the 2 TB cap ON
TRIAL ONLY; paid plans have no egress fees and no egress figure on this page.
"Estimated monthly cost" appears on paid plans only.

THE ESTIMATE IS A GUIDE, NOT THE INVOICE: it applies $4.99/TB to the most recent
storage reading with the monthly minimum as the floor, while the invoice uses
AVERAGE storage across the month, metered twice daily. The estimate excludes
egress. Sizes are decimal (1 TB = 1,000 GB).

## Payment method

Shows last four digits and expiry with "Update", or "No payment method added"
with "Add". "Update" and "Manage plan" both open the STRIPE CUSTOMER PORTAL,
where card details are entered and stored; FIL ONE DOES NOT HOLD THE CARD NUMBER.
First-time setup goes through "Choose your plan": "Pay-as-you-go" is
self-service, "Business plan" routes to a sales contact form.

CANCELLATION IS HANDLED IN THE STRIPE PORTAL, via "Manage plan".

## Invoice history

Date, status, amount and a "PDF" link per invoice. The card appears once on a
paid plan (nothing to show during trial), and lists THE THREE MOST RECENT PAID
INVOICES. Full history, including anything open or in draft, is in the Stripe
portal.

## Pricing panel

$4.99 per TB per month, the monthly minimum where one applies, no egress fees, no
API request fees. "Need more?" links to a Business-plan sales form.

THE MONTHLY MINIMUM IS NOT UNIVERSAL: accounts predating it stay on per-unit
pricing with no minimum, and the plan card and pricing panel reflect that. The
upgrade dialog shows the standard "$4.99/month minimum" wording regardless, so
the plan card and pricing panel are authoritative per account.

# App: Settings

Source: https://docs.fil.one/app/settings

Bottom of the left sidebar next to Billing: profile, notification preferences and
account security.

## Profile

| Field | Rules |
|-------|-------|
| Full name | Cannot be empty, up to 200 characters |
| Company name | 2 to 100 characters, letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, periods only |
| Email | Must be a valid address; disposable addresses are rejected |

"Save changes" is disabled until a field is edited, and a note beside it lists
what will be saved.

CHANGING THE EMAIL ADDRESS RESETS VERIFICATION. Saving a new address marks the
account unverified, sends a verification email to the new address, and lands on
the verification screen; every page redirects there until it is confirmed, as for
a new account. The address can be edited again while unverified, so a typo is
recoverable.

GOOGLE AND GITHUB SIGN-INS MANAGE NAME AND EMAIL AT THE PROVIDER. Both fields are
read-only in Fil One, labelled "Managed by Google" / "Managed by GitHub" with a
link to that provider's profile page. COMPANY NAME STAYS EDITABLE on every
account type.

## Notifications

"Marketing emails" ("Receive updates about new features") is a working toggle: it
reflects the current subscription status, is off until turned on, and saves on
flip with no Save button.

"EMAIL NOTIFICATIONS" IS MARKED COMING SOON AND IS NOT ACTIVE YET. The row ("Get
notified about your uploads and when approaching storage limits") is visible but
disabled, and these emails are NOT SENT TODAY, including as a trial cap
approaches. Direct users to the Dashboard usage cards to track storage and egress
against the caps.

## Security

Two-factor authentication, passkeys, recovery codes and password changes are all
under Settings > Security (see Account Security). Password is managed by the
provider on Google and GitHub accounts, so no Change button appears.

## Deleting your account

Handled by the team: email support@fil.one. Not self-service in the console.

# App: Support

Headed "Talk to an expert", stating a typical response within one business day.

address), Category, Message. Category options: "Product Issue", "Billing Issue",
"General Inquiry", "Feature Request".

The form starts empty rather than pre-filling from the signed-in account, so the
email entered is where the reply goes. Submitting clears the form and confirms a

REPLIES ARRIVE BY EMAIL. The message creates a ticket for the support team; the
console does not show a ticket list or status view.

- "Documentation" in the same Help menu opens the docs in a new tab.
- The sidebar links to the Fil One status page, the quickest check for whether an

  Billing page.
